patients.summary: Healthy undergraduate who joined the practice at 19. Treated in the office for gonococcal urethritis in January 2025 and primary syphilis in July 2025; seen in an outside ED for gonococcal proctitis in July 2026, after his last practice visit.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 19 y/o male, college student, looking for a primary doctor close to campus now that he has aged out of his pediatrician. Has the university student health plan; card info taken, membership agreement emailed. No current concerns. Booked new patient visit 9/13 at 9:00. Records release for the pediatric office sent with the welcome packet.

social.value: Social alcohol use (2-3 drinks on weekends)

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
19 y/o man here to establish. Second-year undergrad, lives off campus with two roommates. Was followed by a pediatric office through high school; no ongoing problems, no hospital stays, no operations. Takes nothing daily, not even supplements. No drug allergies.

Family: dad has high blood pressure, found around age 45. Mom has been treated for major depression. No other family history he knows of.

Social: has never smoked. Drinks socially on weekends, usually 2-3 drinks. Denies other substances. Walks everywhere on campus, plays pickup basketball.

ROS: negative across systems today.

Exam: well-appearing, comfortable. Vitals reviewed, BP normal. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rashes. Extremities warm, no edema. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright, PHQ-2 0.

Assessment/plan:
- Healthy young adult, establishing care. Baseline CBC and CMP today since he has never had adult labs.
- Immunizations: pediatric office records requested; will update once we see what he has. Flu and COVID boosters when the fall supply arrives.
- Discussed safer sex and condom use in general terms; he had no questions.
- Given dad's history, BP check at each visit.
- Follow up for a yearly physical next summer.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Gavin, your blood count, kidney and liver tests, sugar and electrolytes from yesterday all came back normal. Nothing to change. Good to meet you, and reach out any time.

documents.title: Immunization record from prior pediatric office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: One-page immunization printout came back from the pediatric office in response to our request. Shows routine childhood series complete, Tdap 10/7/2014 and MenACWY booster 10/2/2018. No visit notes, problem list or growth charts were included. Tdap and MenACWY entered into immunization history. Copy placed in media.

documents.title: Vaccine administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines. Feels well, no fever. No prior vaccine reactions, NKDA. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Pfizer bivalent COVID booster 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. VIS sheets reviewed. Observed 15 minutes, tolerated both, left ambulating.

documents.title: Form for school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, the university health office says my immunization form is missing the doctor signature part for next year's housing. Can you fill it out from what my old doctor sent? I uploaded the blank form. Thanks

documents.title: RE: Form for school
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Gavin, the form is filled out from your record and signed. It is uploaded to your portal documents to download. Let us know if the school needs anything else.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly check before the fall semester. Spent the summer working at a campus library job. No new symptoms or concerns. No meds, no allergies.

Habits: still nonsmoker. Weekend drinking unchanged at 2-3 drinks, AUDIT-C 3. Sleeping 7 hours most nights. Sexually active, says he uses condoms most of the time; declined STI testing today, no symptoms.

Exam: NAD. BP within normal range. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur. Clear lungs. Abdomen benign. Skin clear. No edema. PHQ-2 negative.

A/P: well young adult. Up to date on Tdap and MenACWY per records. Flu vaccine this fall, he will likely get it at the pharmacy near school. Lipids next year. Back in a year.

documents.title: Got my flu shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I got the flu shot at the pharmacy on campus a week ago Saturday, the 14th. They said they would send it to you but just in case.

documents.title: RE: Got my flu shot
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Gavin. Nothing has come from the pharmacy yet, so I entered the 10/14 flu vaccine in your history from your message.

documents.title: Missed your physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Gavin, we missed you at 9:30 this morning for your yearly physical. Reply here or call and we can find you another time before classes start.

documents.title: RE: Missed your physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So sorry, totally slept through it after a late shift. Can I do the 27th in the morning?

documents.title: RE: Missed your physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're on for Tuesday 8/27 at 8:15. Come a few minutes early.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from 8/13. Feels fine. Senior year coming up, working evenings at a restaurant this summer. No symptoms to report. No medicines.

Social: never smoker. Alcohol on weekends, 2-3 drinks, no binges he recalls. PHQ-2 1, says the late shifts make him tired some mornings, mood good.

Exam: comfortable. BP normal. HEENT unremarkable. Neck without nodes. Cardiac exam regular rhythm, no murmurs or gallops. Lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft. Skin normal. Extremities without edema.

Plan:
- Tdap is due, 10 years since 2014; given today.
- Fasting lipid panel this morning given dad's blood pressure history; low risk otherwise.
- Flu and COVID vaccines when the fall stock is in.
- Yearly visit next summer.

documents.title: Tdap administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM left deltoid per PCP order. VIS given. No reaction during observation.

documents.title: Cholesterol results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gavin, your cholesterol panel is normal across the board. We'll recheck in a few years.

documents.title: Vaccine administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Afebrile, well today. NKDA, no past reactions. Trivalent flu 0.5 mL IM to the left arm and 2024-25 Pfizer COVID 0.3 mL IM to the right arm. Waited 15 minutes, no problems.

documents.title: Nurse triage
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called the nurse line first thing. Three days of burning with urination and some white discharge from the penis. No fever, no testicular pain. Had sex without a condom with a new partner about two weeks ago. Offered 11:40 today with PCP, accepted. Asked him not to have sex until he has been seen.

medications.sig: 500 mg IM once, given in office
Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 7 days

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-day visit: urethral symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22 y/o M seen same day for 3 days of dysuria with a whitish penile discharge. About two weeks ago had unprotected sex with a partner he had not been with before. No fever, no rash, no joint aches, no testicular pain, no sores he has noticed. Otherwise healthy, no regular medicines, NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. No rash on trunk, palms or soles. No cervical or inguinal adenopathy. Joints without swelling. GU: clear discharge at the urethral meatus; no ulcers or other lesions on the penis; testes descended, nontender, no swelling or mass.

UA in office: LE positive, nitrite negative; micro 10-15 WBC/hpf, 0-2 RBC/hpf.

A/P: acute urethritis, most likely gonococcal given the picture.
- First-void urine NAAT for gonorrhea and chlamydia sent.
- Not waiting on the result: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given here, and doxycycline 100 mg BID x 7 days until chlamydia is ruled out.
- No sex for 7 days after treatment and until partner is treated. Partner should get tested; he says he can reach that partner.
- Will call him with the NAAT.

documents.title: Medication administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM right ventrogluteal per PCP order. Tolerated. Observed 20 minutes, no reaction. Doxycycline e-prescribed to his pharmacy; reminded to take with a full glass of water and stay upright for a while after.

documents.title: Result call: gonorrhea NAAT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with Gavin. Urine NAAT positive for gonorrhea, negative for chlamydia. He already had the ceftriaxone, so treatment is done; ok to stop the doxycycline since chlamydia is negative. Burning already easing. Reviewed partner notification again; he will tell the partner today so they can be tested and treated. Abstain 7 days. Gonorrhea is reportable; case report sent to the state health department. Call if symptoms persist past a week.

documents.title: Sore
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I have a sore on my penis. It doesn't hurt at all but it's been there like a week and isn't going away. Can someone look at it today?

documents.title: RE: Sore
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes, we can see you today at 2:20 with your PCP. Please avoid sexual contact until you've been seen.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-day visit: genital ulcer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back about six months after he was treated for gonococcal urethritis. Now has a sore on the penis that came up roughly three weeks after condomless sex with another new partner. It does not hurt and he has had nothing else: no discharge, no burning, no rash, no fevers. The January symptoms went away within a few days of treatment and never came back. No medicines, NKDA.

Exam: well-appearing, afebrile. Single ulcer on the penile shaft, sharply marginated, firm and indurated at the base, painless to touch, clean base. No inguinal nodes on either side. No rash on trunk, palms or soles. Mouth without lesions. The rest of the exam is normal.

A/P:
1. Painless indurated genital ulcer, clinically a primary chancre. Treating today rather than waiting: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM once (no penicillin allergy). Labs: RPR, FTA-ABS, HIV Ag/Ab, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody.
2. Second STI in six months with new partners and inconsistent condoms. Added high risk sexual behavior to the problem list. Talked through condoms with every new partner and testing every few months while this continues.
3. Prior gonococcal urethritis: treated, resolved, off the active list.
- Abstain until the sore is fully healed and at least 7 days after treatment. Partner(s) from the last 3 months need testing and treatment.
- Repeat RPR in about 6 months.

documents.title: Medication administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Bicillin L-A 2.4 million units given as two 1.2 million unit injections, one in each ventrogluteal site, per PCP order. Patient tolerated well. Watched 30 minutes. Reviewed that some people get fever, aches or chills in the first day after the shot and that this passes on its own.

documents.title: Your results from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gavin, the RPR (syphilis screening test) is positive, which fits the sore and the shot you already got. Your HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests are all negative. The confirmatory syphilis test is still running and I'll let you know when it's back. No more treatment is needed beyond what you had yesterday.

documents.title: RE: Your results from yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thanks. I told the person I was with

documents.title: FTA-ABS result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FTA-ABS reactive, confirming primary syphilis. Called him: he is feeling well, sore already smaller. Reviewed plan for RPR at 6 months. Syphilis case report submitted to the state health department with the treatment date.

documents.title: Call from public health nurse
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Disease intervention nurse from the state health department called to confirm the treatment for the syphilis report. Confirmed benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 7/28/25. She will be contacting the patient directly about partner services.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal influenza vaccine, trivalent, 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Screening questions negative. Declined COVID booster today, will think about it. No immediate reaction.

documents.title: Time for your follow-up blood test
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Gavin, it has been about six months since your treatment in July, so it's time for the follow-up visit and RPR blood test. We have openings the first week of February. Reply with a day that works.

documents.title: RE: Time for your follow-up blood test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Tuesday the 3rd after 3 works

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up after syphilis treatment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check after benzathine penicillin for primary syphilis on 7/28/25. The sore healed within a couple of weeks and he has had no new sores, rash, hair loss, headaches or vision change. No urinary symptoms. Says he has been more careful with condoms since the summer.

Exam: well. Genital skin without ulcer or scar of note. No inguinal nodes. No rash on palms or soles.

A/P: primary syphilis, treated. RPR today to document the response. Continue condoms; STI testing at the yearly physical or sooner with any symptoms or new partners.

documents.title: RPR result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, Gavin: your RPR is now non-reactive, which is what we hope to see after treatment. I've moved the syphilis to your past history. The other syphilis test (FTA-ABS) usually stays positive for life, so if anyone ever tests you, let them know you were treated in July 2025.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23 y/o here for his yearly. Still finishing his degree, one more semester. Feels well. No genital sores, discharge or dysuria since last winter's follow-up. No medications. NKDA.

Past history: gonococcal urethritis 1/2025 and primary syphilis 7/2025, both treated; RPR non-reactive in February.

Social: no tobacco ever. Weekend drinking, 2-3 drinks. Sexually active with new partners at times; condoms most but not all of the time.

Exam: healthy-appearing. BP in normal range. HEENT clear. No lymphadenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft and nontender. Genital exam normal, no lesions. Skin without rash. No edema. PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
- Routine physical, well.
- High risk sexual behavior: STI screen today with HIV, RPR, urine gonorrhea/chlamydia. Reinforced condom use and testing with symptoms or new partners.
- Vaccines current; flu this fall.
- Yearly follow-up.

documents.title: Screening results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Gavin, your HIV test, RPR, and urine tests for gonorrhea and chlamydia from Friday are all negative. Have a good summer.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit date: 07/25/2026, arrival 13:10
Patient: Gavin Davidson, 23 y/o M
Allergies: no known drug allergies
Home medications: none

CC: rectal pain with discharge x 1 week.

HPI: 23-year-old man with a past history of gonococcal urethritis and primary syphilis, both treated, presenting with a week of rectal pain, a mucopurulent discharge from the anus and blood on and off, along with tenesmus. Also anal itching. Defecation is painful. Reports condomless sex with more than one partner including receptive anal sex, most recently about two weeks ago.

PMH: gonococcal urethritis; primary syphilis. PSH: none. FH: father hypertension (onset 45); mother major depression. SH: never smoker; social alcohol on weekends; college student.

Vitals: within normal limits throughout the stay.

Exam: uncomfortable-appearing but nontoxic. Abdomen soft, nontender. Perianal skin intact. Anal canal erythematous and tender, with a small amount of purulent discharge. No palpable masses. Prostate nontender on DRE.

Labs: WBC 12.0 K/uL. RPR non-reactive. HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab non-reactive. Rectal swab sent for gonorrhea and chlamydia NAAT.

MDM: presentation consistent with infectious proctitis in the setting of receptive anal exposure; gonococcal most likely. Treated empirically in the department.

ED course: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given. Discharged with doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 7 days.

Addendum 07/27/2026 09:40: rectal NAAT positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Patient already treated. Chlamydia result not available at time of this addendum.

Diagnosis: gonococcal proctitis.
Disposition: discharged home. Abstain from sex for 7 days after treatment and until partners are treated. Follow up with primary care physician within 1-2 weeks.

documents.title: Went to the ER this weekend
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know I went to the emergency room Saturday for pain and some bleeding from my rear end. They said it's probably gonorrhea again, gave me a shot and doxycycline for a week. They told me to see my regular doctor. Already feeling better.

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER this weekend
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, Gavin. I'm glad it's settling. Finish all of the doxycycline and hold off on sex until a week after the last dose and until your partners are treated. We're asking the hospital for the ER record. The front desk will reach out to set a follow-up visit.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed records request with signed release to the regional hospital ED for the 7/25/26 visit. Patient booked for follow-up Wednesday 9/2/26 at 3:00, first opening that fits his schedule.

documents.title: ED record received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED provider note with addendum and lab page for 7/25/26 received by fax after a second request. Filed under outside records and routed to PCP inbox for review at the 9/2 visit.
